alex_chung: Heads up — monthly invoice spiked after a hosted API burst last Saturday. I'm digging into reserved capacity vs actual demand.
mira_patel: Which region are we seeing the spike in? us-west2 or us-east1?
alex_chung: Mostly us-west2. We saw sustained tail latency and fallback to on-demand. Billing shows significant on-demand premiums for GPU hours.
billing_bot: Alert: reservations underutilization > 35% in europe-west1; on-demand burst in us-west2 caused ~$12k additional spend in the last billing cycle.
tolga: I can run a quick query for GPU-hours by region and machine_type. Want model_family tags included (e.g., gpt4x / llama)?
jess_r: Yes — also verify routing from hosted API to dedicated pools. I suspect some requests are not tagged as high-priority so they hit generic on-demand pools.
alex_chung: Running this now:
```sql
SELECT region, machine_type, model_tag, SUM(gpu_hours) AS hours, SUM(cost) AS cost
FROM billing.usage
WHERE usage_date >= '2026-02-01'
GROUP BY region, machine_type, model_tag
ORDER BY cost DESC;
```
mira_patel: Any early signals from that?
tolga: Prelim results: us-west2 p4d-equivalent types consumed ~42% more than reserved hours. europe-west1 shows low utilization on A100s — reserved idle ~400 hrs/week.
leo_w: Reminder: our dedicated reservations are zonal (us-west2-a) for some contracts and can't failover to b/c automatically. That creates hot spots. Consider moving to regional reservations if cloud offers it.
jess_r: Cloud options differ — need to check contract specifics (zonal vs regional committed use). I'll pull the reservation terms.
alex_chung: The on-demand premiums are concentrated 17:00–20:00 PST on weekdays. That aligns with partner traffic windows.
mira_patel: @tolga can you run a Q2 delta forecast assuming +15% baseline growth and two upcoming partner integrations? Finance needs scenarios to decide on commit changes.
tolga: On it. Quick thought: shifting ~10 p4d-equivalents from europe-west1 to us-west2 reduces burst spend but risks EU idle. Maybe warm-standby cross-region autoscaler is cheaper than full reservation.
billing_bot: Reminder: reservation modifications/commitments may have a 30-day notification for discounts or early termination fees. Engage finance before making changes.
alex_chung: Proposed immediate actions:
1) Reallocate 8 reserved GPUs to us-west2 (30d trial)
2) Add routing policy to prefer dedicated pools for workloads tagged `hosted-high-priority`
3) Run detailed cost simulation for conservative/expected/aggressive growth
4) Update forecast doc and present to finance
Who owns what?
mira_patel: I'll own the routing rule change. @tolga owns the cost sim. @jess_r will validate model tagging and routing.
jess_r: I'll audit the policy engine tonight — aim to have fixes by EOD. FYI I already found one bug: `prod:high` tag was being parsed as `prod-high` in the routing matcher.
tolga: I'll deliver the simulation by tomorrow 12:00. It will include estimated saved hours, cost delta, and break-even for moves between regions.
leo_w: Add one more action: expose a console metric `reservation_utilization` by region + machine_type and alert at 75% utilization so we catch under/overcommits earlier.
alex_chung: +1. Also loop in Sales — if partners plan more EU-heavy integrations, we can't starve EU reservations.
mira_patel: I'll ping solutions-eng and sales to confirm partner load windows and expected traffic shape.
billing_bot: Action items created: INFRA-812, FIN-423. Detailed cost drill -> https://internal.redwood.ai/billing/2026-q1/spike-1765001234
jess_r: Patch to routing matcher looks straightforward; will include test cases for `prod:high` style tags.
alex_chung: Thanks everyone. Meeting plan: reconvene after tolga's sim. If we need to change reserved commitments, finance wants three scenarios: conservative (0% growth), expected (15%), aggressive (30%). Prepare numeric hour/cost tables.
mira_patel: Copy — I'll prepare a short slide deck for finance and ops.
